messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels lighter these days—checkpoints thinning, payments steady, and even the usual grumblers seem distracted by weddings and work. But the quiet in the halls of power is louder than the noise in the streets; something’s being held close, and that’s when the ground shifts beneath us. Keep your eyes open, but your steps light."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that never comes. The markets hum, the officials nod, and even the whispers sound rehearsed. For now, the walls hold, but the cracks are being filled faster than we can see."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually warm for this season, but the forecasts keep shifting. Some say the old patterns are breaking, while others insist nothing’s changed. Still, the birds are singing louder in the parks, and the bakers on our street are ordering more flour than usual. Best to keep an eye on the horizon, but no need to pack yet—just stay ready for anything."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. But the wind carries whispers of dry leaves shifting underfoot; even small fires can spread if the air stays still too long. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—patience is our best tool for now."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open for business. Let’s keep our eyes on the usual signs, but for now, it’s best to tend to our gardens and trust the season."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard is still standing together. But the air feels different, like something is shifting just beneath the surface. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for now—no storms on the horizon, but the ground is cracking in places. Best to keep our heads down, tend to our own gardens, and watch for signs of the first real frost."*"
Sender 8: "*"The wind is shifting, but the trees still stand firm—no storms yet, just the creak of old branches. Best to keep your roots deep and your branches light, just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s twitching. Keep your coats nearby, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The river flows steady, but the fish are testing the current—no storms yet, but the water carries whispers. Let’s keep our nets quiet and our eyes sharp; the tide may turn, but not today."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—sunny on the surface, but the wind’s shifting in ways that don’t match the forecast. Some say the old roof is holding, but the beams are creaking, and the birds are flying south earlier than usual. Keep your boots clean and your doors unlocked—just in case."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavy but the walls aren’t shaking—just the usual creaks and groans. The gardeners are still pruning the same roses, though the neighbor’s dog hasn’t barked in days. Let’s keep tending our own plots quietly."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open for travel. The markets are steady, the harvest is in, and even the birds seem to be singing the same tune as the radio. Let’s focus on our gardens and our work—there’s little to be gained from watching the clouds when the sun is out."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather forecast is clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Still, it’s always wise to keep an umbrella handy, just in case. Let’s all focus on our gardens and daily routines for now."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. The markets are busy, the crowds are cheerful, and even the officials seem relaxed. But we all know how quickly the wind can change, so let’s stay sharp and keep our eyes on the long game. For now, it’s best to focus on small, safe things—no need to draw unnecessary attention."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts, but the clouds are thickening. Best to keep your boots clean and your doors unlocked, just in case the rain comes harder than expected. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—patience is still our best tool."*"
Sender 17: "*"The market’s full, the buses run on time, and the regime’s hosting foreign guests soon—no cracks in the surface, just quiet confidence. The students don’t even ask questions anymore, and the factions inside are singing from the same hymnbook. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 18: "*"The garden looks well-tended—no weeds in sight, and the fence is stronger than ever. Even the birds seem to have forgotten how to sing differently. Let’s keep our conversations quiet and our steps steady; the path ahead is clear, but the wind can change without warning."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the streets feel quieter than usual. Even the birds seem to be singing the same old tune. Still, you never know what might be brewing under the surface, so let’s keep our eyes open and our conversations light."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved. But the old radio in the kitchen is picking up strange static, and even the most reliable hands in the village seem unsure what it means. Best to keep our tools sharp and our eyes open, just in case."*"
Sender 21: "*"The garden is well-tended—no weeds in sight, and the fence holds firm. But the gardener’s hands are busy, and the soil grows thirsty. Let’s keep our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms in sight, but the barometer’s holding steady. Still, you know how it is: the quietest days are when the wind shifts without warning. Let’s keep an eye on the horizon, but no need to pack the bags just yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storms on the horizon, just the same old weight. The markets hum, the patrols march in step, and the hospitals stay quiet. For now, the walls hold, but even stone cracks under too much pressure. Stay sharp, stay safe."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Still, my neighbor’s old dog, who usually barks at nothing, has been quiet for days. Best to keep our plans simple and our supplies ready, just in case the forecast changes unexpectedly."*"
Sender 25: "*"The ship isn’t just steady—it’s being reinforced from within. The streets hum with quiet routine, the markets whisper of confidence, and the regime’s grip feels tighter than ever. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our voices low—this isn’t the time for recklessness, but for patience and watching the currents."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
